comparison: Perfect agreement on methodological approach (C2-C5, C27-C40, C116-C121). Both evaluations find the statistical rigor, data generation, and sensitivity analyses well-supported. OpenEval provides more technical detail about specific methodological elements, while peer review emphasizes the 'comprehensive, hypothesis-free approach' with 'solid evidence backed by robust data.'

Complete agreement on platform development (C6, C26, C41-C42, C122). Both evaluations support the MRAD database claims. OpenEval notes the novelty claim (C26) cannot be independently verified but accepts the platform's features. Peer review affirms it as 'an advancement' and 'very convenient, free as well as user-friendly tool' without questioning novelty.

Agreement on the 80 trait findings (C43-C47). Both evaluations support these associations. OpenEval raises a methodological note about the p<0.05 threshold being permissive given multiple testing, though acknowledges Bonferroni correction elsewhere. Peer review accepts findings as part of 'thorough and comprehensive evaluation' without specific statistical concerns.

Agreement on lipid associations (C48-C56). Both evaluations support these findings. OpenEval notes the need for complete effect sizes and confidence intervals, and mentions alignment with established AD research. Peer review accepts findings as part of overall robust data without specific critique of lipid results.

Strong agreement on CD33 findings (C7, C64-C65, C73-C83). Both evaluations support CD33 as a therapeutic target. OpenEval notes convergence with prior GWAS and functional studies but observes reliance on cited literature rather than new mechanistic data. Peer review emphasizes 'great clinical and scientific significance' and accepts CD33 as a novel therapeutic target without critique.

Partial overlap on immunological findings. OpenEval addresses C57-C58 (immunological traits) which appear in peer R5, but peer R5 primarily focuses on CD33 (C7, C64-C65, C73-C83). Both are grouped under immunological/therapeutic findings but emphasize different aspects.

Agreement on C-reactive protein findings (C59-C60). OpenEval supports the associations but notes the negative association contradicts some prior literature and warrants discussion. Peer review rates as UNCERTAIN, with editor noting need for 'more rigorous validation of associations,' potentially referencing unexpected findings like the CRP result.

Complete agreement on TBCA findings (C8, C67, C84-C90). Both evaluations support TBCA as a protective factor and therapeutic target. OpenEval emphasizes stringent statistical significance and convergent evidence while noting experimental validation would strengthen claims. Peer review accepts findings as part of novel therapeutic targets without specific concerns.

Complete agreement on VPS29 findings (C9, C68, C91-C100). Both evaluations support VPS29 as a therapeutic target. OpenEval provides detailed mechanistic rationale through retromer function and cites supporting literature. Peer review accepts findings as part of comprehensive evaluation without raising concerns about VPS29 associations or mechanistic interpretations.

Complete agreement on GNAI3 findings (C10, C69, C101-C104). Both evaluations support the associations. OpenEval notes differential associations between LOAD and EOAD and observes limited mechanistic explanation. Peer review accepts GNAI3 among novel therapeutic targets as part of comprehensive findings backed by robust data.

Complete agreement on PSME1 findings (C11, C70, C107-C113). Both evaluations support PSME1 as a therapeutic target. OpenEval notes the biological rationale through proteasome function and differential LOAD/EOAD associations requiring further validation. Peer review accepts findings without specific concerns as part of comprehensive evaluation with clinical significance.

Agreement on family history associations (C61-C62). Both evaluations support these findings. OpenEval raises an important methodological concern that family history may violate MR assumptions by reflecting both genetic and environmental factors. Peer review accepts findings as aligning with established AD heritability knowledge without questioning the methodological approach.

Divergence on dementia/neurodegenerative disease categorization (C63). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, raising concerns about reverse causality, shared pathophysiology, and diagnostic overlap when using other dementias as exposures for AD. Peer review rates as SUPPORTED, accepting the categorization as part of comprehensive evaluation without questioning these methodological issues.

Agreement on lifestyle trait findings (C72). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN due to lack of specific details about which traits, directionality, or effect sizes, noting the manuscript should provide complete details. Peer review rates as SUPPORTED, accepting lifestyle factors as part of thorough evaluation without raising concerns about specificity.

Divergence on inconsistent findings (C66, C71). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting inconsistency between main outcomes and AD subtypes suggests heterogeneity or statistical artifacts requiring investigation. Peer review rates as SUPPORTED (C71 only), accepting transparent reporting of null findings without concerns about inconsistency patterns.

Agreement on European ancestry limitation (C114-C115). Both evaluations support the authors' acknowledgment of this constraint. OpenEval emphasizes this substantially limits global applicability while praising transparency. Peer review implicitly references this through editor's note about methodological concerns, accepting it as a known constraint without specific criticism.

Agreement on background/epidemiological context (C12-C17). Both evaluations support these literature-based claims. OpenEval notes these are established knowledge providing context rather than novel findings. Peer review accepts background material without question, with partial overlap on claims C12-C17.

Agreement on prior associations and MR rationale (C18-C21). OpenEval supports the review of prior work and critique of observational epidemiology as appropriate context for MR methodology. Peer review implicitly accepts this rationale through praise of 'genetic instruments and analysis' approach, with partial overlap on claims C18-C21.

Agreement on MR methodological principles (C22-C25). OpenEval supports the MR principles and OpenGWAS database description, noting the 'largest database' claim may be time-sensitive. Peer review implicitly accepts methodological framework through praise of comprehensive approach, with partial overlap on claims C22-C25.

Agreement on definitional statement (C1). OpenEval supports this as accurate basic context representing established knowledge. Peer review accepts background material without question, with minimal overlap on claim C1 only.
